One needs to consider core government programs (infrastructure, health, etc.) against non-core programs in order to make informed funding allocations that mitigate the tax burden.

e-bikes.comment: Any vehicle that is not 100% dependent on human propulsion and uses the road, regardless of speed or weight, needs to be licensed along with the driver. The same could be said for horse and buggies.

bike-racks.comment: Maybe bike clubs could buy bike racks and install them where they are needed. You are the users, you know where they need to go - get permission from the land owner and do it.

master-plan.comment: I am an avid user of active transportation and want to support it as much as possible.

spend-more.comment: We need to maintain what we currently have, and many volunteer groups (i.e. Elmira Lions) do a great job with our local trails and other means of active transport. I would support further spending that measurably cuts the need for driving trips and other non-active modes of transport.

propose-initiatives.comment: I believe in the power of community and presence. Initiatives can include large group rides and events to raise awareness for riders, rollers, and walkers of all kinds.

priorities.comment: Enhancing the existing paths between destinations like the St. Jacobs market and village, as well as St Jacobs village to Elmira. Those are not desirable paths (other than Health Valley trail but that could use some love, and better signage for moving people from the market to town).

bike-share.comment: This is a Regional contract, but I like cheaper non-electric bikes and affordable memberships, especially for older riders who aren't comfortable on e-scooters. If a municipal model can work without a big new cost to taxpayers, I'd support it.

snow-clearing.comment: In a rural township, I'd start with the routes that carry real winter traffic, like school routes and the village cores. I'd want to see the cost before committing to a blanket standard, then clear the busiest routes on the same schedule as the roads beside them.

e-bikes.comment: I'd pair wider access with simple trail etiquette signs so walkers and riders know how to share the space.

bike-racks.comment: I'd start simple, with good racks where people actually go: the St. Jacobs village core, the Market, parks, the library and the Woolwich Memorial Centre. We could invite local businesses to sponsor racks outside their doors, which keeps the cost down and helps their customers.

spend-more.comment: I'm very much in favour of funding active transportation, but I would want to be sure that the funding is strategic and effective.  I'm particularly interested in connecting communities safely.

priorities.comment: There should be routes through the township that allow enough space for cyclists (and buggies) and motorists to share the same road.  Lines are ok, and signage helpful, but there needs to be enough paved width for safety.  This may be accomplished with a mix of regional and township roads.  The routes should provide a paved piece of lane, not shared with cars,  to safely connect all settlements in the Township and into the cities.

bike-share.comment: Realistically as a Township councillor I will have no vote at the region, and could only provide input to the mayor who may or may not be receptive.

snow-clearing.comment: I feel like this is a complicated question.  If the weather gets too bad, maybe it's best to switch to skiis.  I would support proper and  timely clearing in the shoulder seasons for sure.  I would support extending the effective clearing season, and seeing utilization.  I'm not sure how relevant this would be to the Woolwich Township situation.  I think winter biking may only be practical in the dense urban areas.

e-bikes.comment: I would really like to see safe connections between communities.  As an example of what is NOT good...when Shantz Station Rd was re-paved, the width of the roadway was decreased, and the white line moved farther from the centre, and there is no longer a wide enough space on the shoulder, outside the white line, to cycle safely.

bike-racks.comment: I wonder if AI surveillance technology could help monitor, and alert when bikes are being cut off of racks, instead of properly unlocked by their rightful owners.  It's a tough problem.  Employers and stores could be encouraged or even incentivized to provide supervised internal space.

master-plan.comment: I support implementing the Active Transportation Master Plan where projects demonstrate clear safety, connectivity and community benefit, while considering affordability and competing infrastructure priorities.

spend-more.comment: I support appropriate investment in active transportation, but I don’t believe simply spending more should be the goal. We should prioritize projects that improve safety and close meaningful gaps in the network, coordinate them with planned road and development work where possible, and make sure residents receive good value for their tax dollars.

propose-initiatives.comment: Yes. I would support practical, community-driven initiatives that improve pedestrian and cycling safety and connectivity, particularly where growing communities have gaps in sidewalks, trails or safe connections to schools, parks and community amenities.

priorities.comment: Focus on completing the most important gaps in our existing network rather than building disconnected infrastructure. Priorities should include safer connections between neighbourhoods, schools, parks and community amenities; addressing pedestrian and cycling safety on higher-speed roads; and ensuring active transportation is incorporated efficiently into new development and planned road reconstruction. In a large rural township, solutions also need to recognize that different communities have different transportation needs and that investments should be practical, equitable and financially responsible.

bike-share.comment: I’m open to considering a municipal bike-share model if the evidence shows it would provide better affordability, accessibility and value for residents. Before committing to a particular operating model, I would want to understand the costs to taxpayers, demonstrated demand, expected utilization and how it would serve communities across the Region—not only the urban core.

snow-clearing.comment:
I support reliable winter maintenance of major cycling routes, particularly routes that serve as important transportation connections. Before committing to a specific 24-hour service standard, I would want to understand the additional cost, operational requirements and actual winter usage. Any enhanced standard should be targeted, practical and provide good value for taxpayers.

Prioritize the highest-use and most important cycling connections rather than applying the same service level everywhere. Where possible, winter maintenance should be coordinated with road clearing so bike lanes are not used for snow storage, and problem locations such as intersections, crossings and trail connections should receive particular attention. Clear service standards and timely communication about route conditions would also help residents make safe travel decisions.

e-bikes.comment:
Yes. I support treating conventional, bicycle-style e-bikes similarly to regular bicycles where they meet appropriate provincial safety, speed and weight standards. E-bikes can make cycling more accessible to more residents, including older adults and people travelling longer distances. Regulations should still prioritize pedestrian safety and allow appropriate restrictions on particular trails or locations where conflicts arise.

Clear and consistent rules across municipalities would help residents understand where different types of e-bikes and other mobility devices can safely operate. I would also support reviewing speed limits on shared-use trails, improving signage where cyclists and pedestrians share space, and ensuring regulations distinguish conventional e-bikes from heavier or faster motorized vehicles.

bike-racks.comment: I would support adding secure bicycle parking at municipal facilities, parks, community centres and other high-use destinations where there is demonstrated demand. Where possible, bike racks should be incorporated into new developments and facility upgrades rather than added later at greater cost. For locations with higher usage or longer-term parking needs, enclosed lockers or cages could be considered based on demand, available space and cost.
